sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Medical Record (EMR) Clinical Workflow Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law with commercial law codification and substantial common-law influence in maritime and financial practice

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 25 of 1995 on Private Interest Foundations; Law 23 of 2015 on AML/CFT (as amended by Law 70 of 2019 and Executive Decree 406 of 2021); Executive Decree 129 of 2021 establishing the Panamanian Beneficial Ownership Registry; Regulation of the Financial Intelligence Unit (UAF) on Legal Person Risk Classification.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Private Interest Foundation Charter (Acta Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary authority in the incorporator's jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or, for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions, Consular Legalization through the nearest Panamanian consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foundation Regulations (Reglamento de la Fundación), if separate from the charter
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary authority in the jurisdiction of execution

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the beneficial owner's passport and proof of residential address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent public authority or licensed bank in the beneficial owner's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified business reference letter from an existing licensed financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or financial institution regulated in the origin jurisdiction

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP and sanctions screening against the Panamanian Financial Intelligence Unit (UAF) risk classification, OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Panama's national sanctions and PEP registers. All UBOs, directors, resident agent personnel, and signatories must be screened before engagement; enhanced due diligence applies to politically exposed persons, high-risk jurisdictions, and politically exposed legal entities.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – Sistema de Consulta de Nombres (SIRG / e-consulta)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names may be in Spanish, English, or any language expressed in Latin script; all non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin characters. The name must not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered foundation, corporation, limited liability company, or other legal entity, and must not misrepresent the foundation's purpose or mislead as to its regulated status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 5 business days of a name rejection, the applicant or resident agent may file a written reconsideration request (recurso de reconsideración) with the Dirección General del Registro Público. If denied, an appellate remedy (recurso de apelación) may be filed within 5 business days. The petition must cite the foundation's draft charter, distinguish the conflicting name, and provide documentary evidence of legitimate business purpose. Upon final denial, a new name may be resubmitted immediately.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not permissible as the registered office of a Panama Private Interest Foundation. A physical Panamanian registered office address and locally licensed resident agent are mandatory. The resident agent must maintain physical custody of statutory records and be physically available for government inspections. The medical EMR software business may use a separate operational virtual office solely for cloud-based correspondence and marketing, provided the statutory registered office remains physical.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for foundation premises, estimated 10% annual probability; moderate for resident agent records, estimated 20% annual probability for unannounced UAF inspections and registry audits of AML/CFT files.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and clearance search fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry fee per certified name search

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff and prevailing legal drafting market fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial registration fee of the Private Interest Foundation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory UBO filing fee and resident agent processing fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory certification fees per document set

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Ley sobre Fundaciones de Interés Privado), as amended by Ley No. 54 de 2004; principal provisions on constitution and purpose (Articles 1–7), minimum initial capital (Article 8), Foundation Council and Protector (Articles 13–18), and registration at the Public Registry (Articles 19–26).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acta Constitutiva (Foundation Charter) executed as a private instrument authorized by a licensed Panamanian attorney or as a notarized public deed, submitted together with the foundation registration form (Formulario de Inscripción) and the registered agent's acceptance letter.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum stated initial capital of US$10,000.00 (B/.10,000.00) under Article 8 of Law 25 of 1995, satisfiable with cash, assets, credits, or intellectual property rights; no escrow account or on-shore bank deposit is required at formation, and the capital is evidenced by a capital inventory (Inventario de Bienes) retained at the registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Pro-Forma First Foundation Council Resolution on Subscription, Registered Office and Officers. RESOLVED: (1) The Foundation Charter dated [●] and recorded at the Public Registry of Panama is ratified; the initial capital of US$10,000.00 stated in the capital inventory is accepted as fully subscribed. (2) The foundation's registered office is fixed at the offices of its registered agent, located at [●], Panama. (3) The following officers are appointed: Council Members [●], [●] and [●], Protector [●], and the President and Secretary of the Foundation Council. (4) The Secretary is authorized to execute municipal, tax, banking and data-protection filings, to open and operate collection accounts for EMR subscription fees, and to engage counsel. This resolution takes effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name clearance and drafting of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (name search and reservation portal) assisted by a licensed Panamanian attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Reserve the proposed foundation name, which must include the expression 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or its English equivalent, through the Public Registry's name search and reservation service; then instruct the attorney to draft the Foundation Charter, bylaws, and capital inventory in Spanish or bilingual form.
required_dossiers: Proposed foundation name containing 'Fundación de Interés Privado'
Passport copies of the founder, Council Members, and initial beneficiaries
Corporate charters and power of attorney if the founder is an entity
Statement of initial capital assets or rights of at least US$10,000.00
Identification and domicile of the proposed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is unavailable or rejected, submit two alternate names and request a new reservation; a third-party name objection may be cured by a notarized consent letter from the prior registrant or by selecting a materially different name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of the charter and governance instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública de la República de Panamá (notary) or authorized Panamanian attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Foundation Charter before a Panamanian notary, or as a private instrument authorized by the attorney in accordance with Law 25; obtain the registered agent's written acceptance (Constancia de Aceptación) and the Foundation Council Members' written acceptances; ensure all signatures requiring certification are notarized before filing.
required_dossiers: Executed Foundation Charter
Capital inventory (Inventario de Bienes) reflecting the initial capital
Registered agent acceptance letter
Council Member appointment and acceptance letters
Notarial certification or attorney authorization of signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary declines certification because of incomplete foreign corporate documents, legalize those documents by apostille and re-submit; alternatively, re-execute the instrument with corrected schedules and re-certify.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of government fees and filing at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (electronic Extranet or counter window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the national stamp tax (papel sellado) and the foundation inscription fee; submit the executed charter, registration form, acceptance letters, and the Law 54 de 2004 AML disclosure containing beneficial owner and source-of-funds information; receive the filing receipt (Visto Bueno) with the assigned docket number.
required_dossiers: Original Foundation Charter and notarial certifications
Foundation registration form and fee payment receipts
Registered agent and Council Member acceptances
Law 54 de 2004 AML compliance declaration
Final identification of the beneficial owner and beneficiaries
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a 'Defecto' (defect notice), file the corrective instrument or supplementary information within the granted deadline (generally 5–10 business days) and request priority re-examination to avoid lapse (caducidad) of the filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of certificate of incorporation and extraction of official records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval of the inscription, the Registry assigns the Ficha number and enters the foundation in the mercantile database; request the Certificado de Registro and a certified attestation of the Foundation Council composition; verify that the charter date, foundation name, and identification data match the filed instrument.
required_dossiers: Filing receipt (Visto Bueno)
Paid fee acknowledgement from the Registry
Power of attorney for collection of certificates, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate is delayed beyond the service-level target, file a written expedited-certificate petition with the Registry Directorate; if data errors appear in the inscription, correct them through a notarized corrective deed (instrumento de corrección) and re-register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration (RUC) and municipal business licensing (Aviso de Operación)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DGI – Dirección General de Ingresos (RUC/PAN electronic system) and Municipio de Panamá (Tesorería Municipal / Aviso de Operación window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the foundation in the DGI's Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC-PAN) using Formulario 01 and declare the ISIC 6201 software-services economic activity; file the municipal Aviso de Operación application with the corresponding IT/software activity code and obtain the municipal resolution authorizing operation of the Panama City office.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Registro issued by the Public Registry
Executed Foundation Charter and RUC application form
Proof of Panamanian office address (lease agreement or cadastral certificate)
Identification of Council Members and employee count declaration
Municipal Aviso de Operación application and fee schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI or the Municipality issues a query, correct the declared economic activity or registered address and re-file electronically within the response term; a final denial may be appealed to the National Directorate of Revenues or through the municipal reconsideration remedy (recurso de reconsideración).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipio de Panamá – Dirección de Rentas y Aviso de Operación, in coordination with the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) for technology-sector classification; ancillary authorities include Ministerio de Salud (MINSA), Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá, Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL), Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE), and the Autoridad Nacional de Transparencia y Acceso a la Información (ANTAI) for health data registration under Ley 81 de 2019.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Business Operation Permit) for Professional, Technical and IT Services under Ley No. 66 de 1947 and municipal ordinances; the EMR SaaS activity also requires registration of the health database in the ANTAI National Registry of Personal Data Processing (Ley 81 de 2019) and, where the platform interoperates with Panama's national health information system, compliance with MINSA health-information-system registration requirements.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación de Impacto Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category I – Simplified Environmental Registration (Ficha de Inscripción / Checklist). Office-based software programming (ISIC 6201) is not listed as an activity requiring a full Estudio de Impacto Ambiental under Decreto Ejecutivo No. 123 de 2009; the operator registers the activity with MiAMBIENTE and receives a low-impact environmental certificate.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Domestic wastewater discharged to municipal sewers must comply with Decreto Ejecutivo No. 39 de 2013: pH 6.0–9.0, BOD5 ≤ 350 mg/L, COD ≤ 700 mg/L, TSS ≤ 350 mg/L; electronic waste (RAEE) and spent IT equipment must be segregated and delivered to an authorized e-waste recycler; no significant point-source VOC emissions are generated by office IT activity; standby generators, if installed, must meet national ambient air quality standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá – fire prevention certificate covering extinguishers, emergency exits, alarm systems, evacuation plan, and annual inspection; Municipio de Panamá – building occupancy permit confirming seismic and structural load compliance and approved office use; MINSA – Aviso Sanitario de Funcionamiento for non-health commercial premises; MITRADEL – registration under the national occupational health and safety regulations (COPANIT), including workplace risk assessment, industrial hygiene, and formation of a joint health and safety committee where employee thresholds are met.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas, Republic of Panama. Official self-service portal: https://www.dgi.gob.pa (DGI 'Portal de Trámites y Servicios').
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) procurement for a foreign-owned PIF: (1) Register the foundation charter with the Registro Público de Panamá and maintain the mandatory Panamanian resident agent; (2) File the RUC application (Formulario de Solicitud de RUC) with DGI, attaching certified copies of the registered charter, resident-agent appointment, foundation-council minutes identifying officers, notarized identification of founders/beneficiaries or their designation mechanism, and evidence of the local address of the resident representative; (3) Obtain the RUC number and activate the DGI e-portal account, which is the precondition for ITBMS registration, electronic-invoice authorization, and service-export contract registration. Non-resident founders and beneficiaries are permissible; all official tax notices are served on the resident agent. A PIF deriving only foreign-source income must still maintain an active RUC for banking, AML, and e-invoicing compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope - under the Código Fiscal, the PIF is a separate entity-level taxpayer, but only Panamanian-source income is taxable (standard 25% corporate ISR on domestic profits); foreign-source income from the EMR SaaS licence fees paid by non-resident medical clinics is outside the scope of Panamanian income tax. Law 25 of 1995 additionally exempts the foundation's organization, registration, and asset-holding operation from national taxes, provided it does not carry on active commercial operations in Panama; any domestic Panama sales of the SaaS would be subject to ISR and ITBMS. The PIF is not a statutory pass-through entity, but is fiscally neutral in practice because distributions of foreign-source funds are not taxed in Panama.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists; the functional entity-classification election occurs at formation by choosing the PIF, corporation, or trust form at the Public Registry. Available elections and filings: (i) voluntary early ITBMS registration to perfect exporter status and preserve input-credit refund rights; (ii) registration/certification of each service-export contract with the DGI before issuing 0% invoices; (iii) optional election of the taxed Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime where the PIF creates the required local substance (5% ISR instead of 25%, on qualifying Panama-source service income); (iv) small-taxpayer integral quota regime (Régimen de Cuota Integral) for domestic activities with annual gross income not exceeding B/. 200,000; and (v) informational return on hybrid arrangements under Law 254 of 2021 (BEPS Action 2), applicable where cross-border royalty or financing flows with clinic clients create hybrid mismatches. None of these elections alter the PIF's territorial tax base.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios), Panama's VAT, levied on transfers of movable goods and on services rendered in Panama; general statutory rate 7%, plus a temporary 3-percentage-point surcharge (effective combined rate 10%) maintained since 1 July 2019; 0% rate applies to exports of goods and of qualifying offshore services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. 0 - no de-minimis turnover threshold. Every person performing taxable transactions in or from Panama must register for ITBMS; an exporter of services must register to issue valid 0% invoices and to claim refunds of input ITBMS. A distinct small-taxpayer integral quota regime is available for taxpayers with annual gross income not exceeding B/. 200,000, but full-registrant status remains the operative structure for exporters seeking input-credit refunds.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (Facturación Electrónica) under the DGI's phased programme: each invoice series requires DGI authorization; invoices must be generated in the DGI XML schema with XMLDSIG digital signature and transmitted to the DGI clearance platform for synchronous validation before issuance, with QR/digital stamping on the delivered PDF or printout. Export invoices must display the 0% ITBMS rate and the registered export-contract reference. Foreign-currency billing is permitted, with ITBMS computed in Balboas/USD at the transaction-date exchange rate. Monthly ITBMS returns and export-credit refund petitions are filed electronically through the DGI portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The 0% export rate applies when cumulative conditions are met: (i) the buyer is a non-resident enterprise without a permanent establishment in Panama (e.g., foreign licensed medical clinics); (ii) the EMR SaaS platform is effectively used and consumed entirely outside Panama (offshore hosting, licensing, cloud support, and maintenance qualify); (iii) the service-export contract is registered with the DGI before the first invoice; (iv) the invoice is issued through the cleared e-invoicing channel at 0%; and (v) the proceeds are received through a Panamanian bank as an inward remittance. The same export character supports territorial exclusion of the corresponding service fees from Panamanian ISR.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) - filed via the DGI/VUPE single window for physical goods; for SaaS, the DGI-registered service-export contract file serves as the operative export declaration
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill for goods, or equivalent electronic delivery and usage evidence for SaaS (hosting registry, access logs, uptime and audit reports demonstrating offshore consumption)
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificación de Ingreso de Divisas) issued by the receiving Panamanian bank showing payment from abroad
Zero-rated commercial invoice cleared through the DGI e-invoicing platform with the registered export-contract reference
Certificate of fiscal residence / non-resident status of the foreign client, including attestation that the client maintains no Panamanian permanent establishment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Panama imposes no statutory exchange-control repatriation deadline; the 180-day window is the DGI's customary documentary benchmark for export-proceeds review and refund substantiation. Unwarranted zero-rating or fictitious export contracts trigger: (i) disallowance of the 0% rate with retroactive ITBMS assessment; (ii) denial and clawback of input-credit refunds already paid; (iii) surcharges (recargos) and default interest computed from the original return due date; (iv) administrative fines of approximately 100% to 200% of the tax evaded under the Código Fiscal; (v) suspension of the RUC and electronic-invoicing authorization; and (vi) criminal prosecution for tax fraud (defraudación tributaria) against the foundation's officers for intentional falsification of export documentation. Export refunds remain subject to documentary and bank-ledger audit for up to the full five-year statute of limitations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) as the primary banking regulator; the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) oversees monetary policy with no autonomous central bank issuance function. The National Bank of Panama (Banco Nacional de Panamá) acts as fiscal agent of the Republic and provides banking services to the public sector but does not exercise independent monetary authority. The Decreto de Gabinete No. 98 of 1941, as amended, codifies the U.S. dollar as legal tender and establishes the Banking Law frame.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current and capital account convertibility under Panama's dollarized regime. The U.S. dollar circulates as legal tender alongside the nationally minted balboa (PAB), which is a subsidiary unit at par 1:1. There are no exchange controls, no capital transfer restrictions, and no prior authorization requirements for inbound or outbound funds. Profit remittances by Private Interest Foundations to non-resident beneficiaries are unrestricted once the foundation satisfies its legal tax and AML obligations under Law 25 of 1995 (as amended) and Executive Decree 163 of 1996. The only practical hurdles arise from banking due diligence and the SBP's AML / CFT supervision under Law 42 of 2000, which requires banks to report unusual transactions and verify beneficial ownership.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Panama imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation timeline, or conversion ratio for export proceeds. Under the constitutional monetary system, all receipts—including service export revenue from the EMR SaaS platform—may be freely retained in USD, held in domestic bank accounts, or transferred abroad without central bank authorization. The lack of a consolidated exchange control regime means the 15-day rule and conversion percentages found in some Latin American jurisdictions do not exist. Exporters are nonetheless subject to commercial invoicing standards and the SBP's oversight on transaction value reporting for statistical purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility. Panama does not currently maintain a statutory cross-border electronic money institution (EMI) license; fintech banking functions are restricted to licensed banks or non-bank money remitters supervised by the SBP under the Remitters' Registry (Registro de Empresas Remisoras de Fondos). Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Mercury, Wise Business, Payoneer) generally accept Panamanian entities with transparent UBO disclosure, but they may impose enhanced due diligence on Private Interest Foundations due to the inherent nominee layer. A sociedad de fundación can satisfy these platforms if it presents a full long-form foundation deed, registered nominee declarations, audited financials, and a demonstrable operational tie to the HealthTech sector.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence of a founding board member (Patron) or an authorized officer is generally required for the initial in-person interview and biometric registration at Tier-1 Panamanian banks. Remote opening is permissible on a case-by-case basis where the applying foundation maintains a pre-existing banking relationship with a well-known foreign financial institution; the foreign bank must conduct KYC and send a certified reference to the Panamanian bank. Alternatively, apostilled corporate documents, notarized signature attestation before a Panamanian consul, and secure video-on-boarding with a sworn affidavit can satisfy the bank's internal policy. In all instances, the underlying beneficiary / ultimate beneficial owner must appear in bank records or be identifiable through a clear chain of foundation documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or layered foundation structure using nominee counselors and no direct identification of the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the full foundation deed (acta de constitución) including the beneficiary clauses, notarized resolution of the Foundation Council, current certificate of incumbency, and sworn declarations by nominees identifying the actual principal. Supply a legal opinion from Panamanian counsel confirming the foundation is not used to disguise criminal property and that the UBO list is documented under Law 42 of 2000.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexpected inbound wire transfers that diverge from the presented revenue model or originate from high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit three months of bank statements showing consistent EMR SaaS subscription inflows, notarized client invoices with the merchant agreement under the business model, and a source-of-wealth statement covering all shareholders and beneficiaries. Supplement with audited financial statements and a letter from the lead bank's compliance department explaining the source of any foreign capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing or inadequate statutory license for healthcare data processing (Medical Clinic EMR SaaS) in Panama
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the certificate of registry with the Ministry of Health (MINSA) if the platform processes Panamanian clinical data, or a clear legal opinion that the platform only serves foreign clients and is not subject to MINSA licensing. Also attach the IT security framework under Law 81 of 2019 (Personal Data Protection), the International Organization for Standardization ISO 27001 certificate, and the HIPAA compliance attestation for U.S.-based clinics to substantiate the lawful continuation of the HealthTech business.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The preferred route is a SWIFT MT103 wire transfer to the foundation's operational account using a transparent purpose code such as '38' (non-trade services) or '91' (business services). The sending entity must include the foundation's full legal name, foundation number assigned by the Public Registry of Panama, and the reference to the shareholder loan or capital contribution agreement. For capital injections above USD 10,000, the Panamanian bank will perform extended due diligence on the sending entity, request the underlying transaction documentation, and file a suspicious activity report if any information mismatch appears. To facilitate rapid clearing, the foundation should prepare the following bundle: certificate of good standing, latest financial statements, board resolution authorizing the capital injection, and a clear narrative of the intended use of funds in the EMR SaaS operation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For routine SaaS vendor payments and cloud infrastructure charges, the most efficient rail is the U.S. ACH and Federal Reserve system when the beneficiary is in USD; for non-USD destinations, SWIFT MT103 is the standard clearlink. Larger disbursements, such as procurement of medical-device integrations or licensing of proprietary algorithms, may require a Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) issued by a Panamanian bank through a correspondent bank in the United States or EU. The LC must be tied to a commercial invoice and the Foundation Council's purchase resolution. International disbursements above USD 300,000 per day require SBP supervision and will likely trigger enhanced due diligence on the beneficiary, so the foundation should pre-clear such transactions and maintain auditable evidence of the artificial intelligence and data processing services rendered.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: US Dollar forward contracts against the Panamanian balboa (USD/PAB with 1:1 peg) ; though not needed for parity risk, such instruments are permissible and used to lock in cross-border settlement rates when the foundation invoices in other Latin American currencies.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on the USD/PAB peer group, mainly USD/BRL, USD/MXN and USD/COP, to hedge vendor payments and royalty flows in those markets.
Cross-currency swaps in the USD/CLP or USD/PEN corridor when the foundation holds a structured debt facility or a commercial contract requiring fixed-price local-currency flows.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Private Interest Foundation Annual Government Fee (Annuity) and simple annual maintenance return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, through the licensed registered agent; Public Registry of Panama ancillary record
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year; no extension is available for private interest foundations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly surcharge equal to 10% of the unpaid fee or fraction thereof, capped at 100%; continuing delinquency prevents issuance of good-standing certificates and may lead to administrative strike-off by the Public Registry after repeated nonpayment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Final Beneficial Ownership Confidential Confirmation (sworn declaration of founder, foundation council members, protector if any, and beneficiaries)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Panama Final Beneficial Ownership Registry (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales), kept under the coordination of the Public Registry and the Dirección General de Ingresos
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, on or before the same 31 March deadline as the annual government fee; any transfer or variation in beneficial entitlement occurring during the prior year must be confirmed in the same filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Statutory fines for late or inaccurate UBO confirmation, registry suspension of corporate filings, and personal liability for the registered agent or foundation council member who fails to maintain current beneficial-owner records

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foundation Council annual continuity minute and registered office/agent custody verification (prepared and retained for inspection)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Public Registry of Panama, inspected through the registered agent's Panama registered office; not a separately paid filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, contemporaneously with the 31 March payment deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to evidence an active registered agent or foundation council may cause rejection of registry filings, impairment of legal standing before Panamanian courts, and eventual strike-off following an administrative procedure

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is imposed solely by Law 25 of 1995 on a passive Private Interest Foundation. A mandatory independent audit arises only if the foundation engages in Panama-source commercial activity and is so required by the Dirección General de Ingresos, becomes a licensed Panamanian financial entity, or if the foundation charter expressly mandates an annual certified audit. Third-party financing agreements may also trigger an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB; Panama permits IFRS for SMEs for non-public entities. A passive Private Interest Foundation may maintain simplified accounting records at the discretion of the foundation council, but must apply full IFRS if it becomes financially active or is consolidated in a Panama-licensed group.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must annually validate the final beneficial owner record file by obtaining and confirming natural-person information for the founder, foundation council members, protector if appointed, and all beneficiaries, including residual beneficiaries. Any share of economic interest, substitution of beneficiaries, or change in the protector must be evidenced by a foundation council resolution and filed in the Panama Final Beneficial Ownership Registry within the annual confirmation cycle. No transfer of foundation interests is effective against third parties until the foundation's protocol amendment is registered and the UBO record is updated.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficiaries and Residual Beneficiaries
Register of Protector Appointments and Reserved Founder Powers
Minute Book of Foundation Council Resolutions
Foundation Charter and Protocol Amendment Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150–400 per year for licensed registered agent plus registered office, depending on the corporate service provider
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000–7,500 per year only if an independent audit becomes mandatory or is contractually required

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% on net taxable income exceeding USD 200,000; 15% on the first USD 200,000
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation: foreign-source income (e.g., EMR SaaS revenue from clients outside Panama) is not subject to Panamanian corporate income tax; no general statutory tax holiday but special incentives may apply to qualifying developments zones or under the Multinational Company Headquarters (SEM) regime; small taxpayer regime may reduce effective rates for certain SME thresholds.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 101 – Declaración Anual de Renta / DGI e-Cho Tax (Panama Tax Administration Digital Portal)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 3 months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., 31 March for a calendar-year taxpayer).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from activities that generate Panamanian-source income, including landing fees, monthly subscriptions, and per-seat EMR software licensing derived from customers located in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only include income sourced in Panama. Foreign SaaS subscriptions (client servers or use outside Panama) should be excluded from Box 1 and reported in an explanatory statement under Box 21; do not inject foreign-source revenue into the Panamanian tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions: direct operating costs (cloud hosting local to Panama, employee salaries, medical-clinic licensing fees, software development costs, and administrative expenses), depreciation, and NOL carryforward claimed within 5-year limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct only expenses that are economically connected to Panamanian-source revenue. Expense allocations must be supported by contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation if affiliated-party transactions exist; foreign-source costs are not allocable to Panama-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after deductions and loss carryforwards, applying the territorial-source limitation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities operating a branch in Panama must allocate taxable income under arm's-length principles and file a branch tax return; the 4% Advance Dividend Tax (ADT) is prepaid on the taxable base regardless of actual dividend distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax at progressive rates: 15% on first USD 200,000; 25% on the excess.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies do not incur Panamanian income tax on foreign-source income; ensure that the tax computation excludes non-territorial revenue and that transfer pricing adjustments are reflected in the Panamanian-source taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Advance Payments, Withholdings and Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for quarterly advance payments (Form 103), the 4% ADT already paid, and any withholding tax on payments credited to the company (e.g., DGI withholding on professional fees).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities are eligible to claim creditable withholding taxes from Panamanian clients only if they comply with registration and retention requirements under the territorial law; refunds for excess ADT are possible through formal petition to DGI.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing fine: 10% of the tax due per month or fraction of delay, capped at 50%; late payment surcharge: 1% per month plus interest (Banco Nacional interest rate); failure to file may lead to default assessment, asset seizure, and criminal liability in cases of fraudulent intent.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 103 – Declaración de Pago Anticipado Trimestral / DGI e-Cho Tax portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on 15 April, 15 July, 15 October, and 15 December for the corresponding quarter of the current fiscal year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as a percentage of the prior year's net income (typically 30% in April and October, 20% in July and December) or a self-assessed estimated current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entities with Panamanian-source profits must compute the instalments using the prior year's Panamanian-source taxable income; foreign-source income is excluded from the base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 4% of the estimated net taxable income for the period, paid as an advance of the 10% dividend withholding tax; credit is applied against final dividend tax when distributions are declared.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot claim a refund of the ADT directly; the Panamanian company may apply the ADT credit on the final Form 101 and corporate distribution of dividends to non-residents is the moment the 10% WHT is settled.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Instalment Tax (Year 1 or prior-year base) + ADT (4% of estimated taxable income) minus any permitted credits; payment is made directly through DGI portal or enabled banks.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the payment is made by the statutory date without fail; if the prior year ended with a PIF company that had zero or negative income, the estimated base is the amount derived in the current period, and declaration of zero or minimal amount must be factually supported.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Underpayment of quarterly instalments triggers interest and a 10% surcharge on the missed amount, plus a fine of 10% of the underpaid amount; failure to file Form 103 three consecutive times disqualifies the taxpayer from the segmented compliance program and can lead to DGI deregistration.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory withholding on dividends paid out of Panamanian-source taxable profits; a 4% Advance Dividend Tax (ADT) is prepaid quarterly and credited against the final 10% WHT.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama maintains a narrow DTA network (e.g., UAE, Colombia, France for shipping, etc.). To claim treaty relief on dividends, the non-resident beneficial owner must file an 'Exoneration y Reducción de Retención' application with the DGI (or via the local payer), provide a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the DTT partner tax authorities, submit a sworn statement of beneficial ownership, and include a legal analysis of the applicable DTA provision. The Panama withholding agent must register the application and obtain DGI confirmation before applying the lower rate; if DGI does not respond within 30 days, the treaty rate cannot be applied defensively, so the payer must withhold at the statutory 10% rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid to non-resident lenders: 6% statutory WHT (reducible under certain DTAs). Royalties and technical service fees for intellectual property used in Panama: 12.5% statutory WHT (reducible under specific AII and semantic licensing cases); treaty rates vary by jurisdiction and require the same TRC procedure.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: USD 3,000,000 – annual aggregate transactions with related parties exceed this threshold, triggering mandatory Local File and Master File under Law 78 of 2017 (Executive Decree 284/2018); entities below the threshold must still maintain contemporaneous evidence if controlled transactions are undertaken.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama Economic Substance Regulations (Law 22 of 2018, Implemented by Executive Decree 352/2019) apply to all entities (including PIFs) engaged in 'relevant activities' in Panama and benefiting from preferential or territorial tax regimes. An EMR SaaS PIF must demonstrate physical presence in Panama — an office, local staff, server/IT assets — and active management decisions executed from Panama to substantiate Panamanian-source revenue. If the PIF operates purely as a passive holding company (fiduciary clause structure) without local substance, it will be exempt from the annual sworn substance filing; but if it argues that foreign SaaS income is outside territorial scope, DGI may challenge the lack of substantive management in the year of loss or low profit and reclassify the entity as a shell, subject to 25% tax and penalties. ESR yearly declaration is mandatory for non-exempt entities; failure to file triggers a USD 10,000 fine and potential strike-off.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Fraudulent Under-Stating of Panama-Source Income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate failure to report or significantly underreporting of medical-clinic subscription revenues from Panamanian customers, fabrication of ICT infrastructure costs, or misclassifying Panamanian-source licensing fees as foreign-source income (e.g., billing via shell office in a no-tax jurisdiction while maintaining code and servers in Panama).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panamanian Fiscal Code (articles 800-802) criminalizes omission of taxes: imprisonment of 2 to 5 years, a fine of up to 100% of the evaded tax, plus 10% monthly surcharge to 50% maximum; DGI may impose a management liability notice and automatic sanction of 10% of the unpaid tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Any officer signing a false return or directing the under-declaration is jointly and severally liable; civil restitution of evaded taxes, travel ban (impedimento de salida), loss of visa status for non-resident directors, and in aggravated cases, pre-trial detention and disqualification from acting as director in Panama for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Abuse of PIF Legal Personality as an Economic Substance Avoidance Vehicle
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Private Interest Foundation as a passive shell to own the EMR SaaS corporate IP and distributing profits without any real employees, office, bank decisions or board meetings in Panama, while claiming that the SaaS revenue is not taxable in Panama because the founder resides in a foreign tax haven.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI and the Financial Superintendence (SUDEB) under Law 22/2018 and Decreto 352/2019 may disregard the PIF (lacking substance), recharacterize its activity as a Panamanian commercial business, and levy the full 25% corporate tax on worldwide-derived EMR SaaS revenue; additional fines up to 200% of omitted tax, strike-off of the PIF from the Registry, and recapture of the 4% ADT as ineffective.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil applies: the president, secretary, and fiduciaries are jointly liable for unpaid taxes and penalties, and can be subjected to civil exclusion, travel bans, and up to 4 years' imprisonment for unlawful underdeclaration; a conviction under Law 23/2015 AML predicates can trigger confiscation of shares and foreign-located assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and AML Non-Compliance in Capital Inflows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting substantial investment from a medical clinic network or health-tech VC fund through opaque channels without performing customer due diligence, failing to file suspicious transaction reports, or handling corporate cloud token revenues in a way that could commingle third-party proceeds (violation of Law 23/2015).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under Law 23/2015 are up to USD 5 million per violation for regulated entities, and illegal concealment of funds amounts to a criminal predicate carrying a sentence of 5 to 12 years in a national penitentiary; the PIF may be dissolved for recidivous violations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are presumed criminally responsible if they fail to observe KYC, registration, and record-keeping obligations; the corporate veil will not shield them from asset freezing, provisional imprisonment, or extradition from if convicted — professional licensure and international travel restrictions also result.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Illegal Dividend Distribution / Inadequate 10% Dividend Withholding
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring and paying dividends to foreign beneficial owners while the 10% dividend WHT is not withheld and remitted to DGI, or paying distributions from non-taxed foreign-source profits without the statutory sworn declaration, or failing to file Form 103 covering the 4% ADT on Panamanian-source profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The corporation is liable to pay the full 10% WHT owed, plus a 50% surcharge for failure to withhold, and a fine of 25% of the distribution amount; DGI may also require immediate closure of bank accounts and could issue a criminal referral for tax fraud under Art. 800.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who votes in favor of an unlawful distribution without confirming DGI payment becomes personally liable for the distribution amount and any resulting criminal fines; criminal prosecution in an aggravated case can lead to 2 to 5 years' imprisonment and a travel ban during the ongoing investigation.
